newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-STANKOWSKI, HART TAKE FIRST-ROUND LEAD IN TEXAS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-STANKOWSKI, HART TAKE FIRST-ROUND LEAD IN TEXAS.

text.p: Paul Stankowski and Dudley Hart shot 64s to tie for a one-stroke lead at the rain-delayed Byron Nelson Classic golf tournament on Thursday.

Stankowski, who played the Tournament Players Course, and Hart, playing across the street at Cottonwood Valley Golf Course, have a one-stroke lead over a large group of golfers, including Tom Watson and Tiger Woods.
Play was delayed for 3-1/2 hours, but Woods, playing in his first tournament since winning the Masters, came out firing after the interruption.
Woods birdied the par-4 first hole with a 10-foot putt, then followed with three straight pars.
Woods turned up the heat for the huge gallery following him by recording birdies on holes five, six, seven and eight. He added a sixth birdie on the par-four 10th hole.
But Woods followed with his first two bogeys of the day at holes 11 and 12 to fall out of the lead.
Stankowski had seven birdies and one bogey in his round. He tied Woods for low nine hole score with a five-under 30. Hart recorded one eagle (the par-5 11th), four birdies and no bogeys.
Tom Watson, a four-time winner of this tournament, led a large group at five-under-par 65.
Mike Standly had a chance to take the lead by himself, but double-bogeyed the par 4 finished hole at the Cottonwood Valley course.
Australian Craig Parry shot a 66 and was one shot back of the early leaders.
Watson said his conquered his struggles with his putting at least in the first round.
"I putted pretty well except for the last hole," Watson said. "I've tried just about everything on my putting, and I made a lot of them today."
Playing the par 70 Cottonwood Valley, Watson shot 32 on the front nine and 33 on the back. He recorded seven birdies, on holes one, six, seven, 11, 12, 13 and 14 and two bogeys on holes three and 18.
"I love this game too much to every want to quit it," Watson said. "I'm going to just keep plugging away and working on my putting."
Scotland's Sandy Lyle shot a solid 71 and was six shots back of the leaders.
Nick Faldo was one-under 34 after nine holes.
Parry, who finished second at this tournament last year, said he was pleased with his first-round play.
"Anytime you can shoot four-under in the first round you have to be pleased," he said. "I missed some short putts, but I feel I'm still in the hunt."
Lyle, who opened with a 66 in his last tournament, two weeks ago in Greensboro, recorded three birdies, two bogeys and one double bogey in his round.
"It wasn't too bad today," Lyle said. "I had some chances at birdie and missed some tiddlers. I did a lot of damage to myself on three holes (7-8-9), but was proud the way I came back."
He shot a four-over 39 on the front nine, but finished with a three-under 32 on the back.
